findings.finding: An open, effective $50M at-the-market program (Evercore, commission up to 3%, S-3 effective 2026-05-27) lets GrafTech sell stock into any rebound during the 2026-09-30 session.
findings.mechanism_in_window: An ATM draws continuously at the issuer's discretion on any trading day, 09-30 included, with no further filing needed before it sells. The company carries $1.2B of 2029 debt, a Q2 net loss of $40M and adjusted EBITDA of $2M, so it has a standing reason to use it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed EAF reaction to an ATM draw. H1 2026 equity proceeds were only $348k (10-Q filed 2026-07-24), so the program has barely been used, and whether it was used during the September run-up is not disclosed until the Q3 10-Q.
findings.why_not_priced: The close prices what has already been sold, not what can be sold into a bounce. The program is $50M against a market cap of about $226M. If the price held it, a rebound after the fall would already be discounted by expected issuance. The small size reflects light historical usage and the fact that a 22% two-day fall makes a draw less attractive to the issuer.
findings.independence: The 10-Q gives the liquidity that motivates issuance: $145.4M cash, $253.0M total liquidity, $1,198.6M long-term debt. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/931148/000093114826000073/gti-20260630.htm

outside_window.finding: Possible overshoot: preliminary AD margins on India (Graphite India 12.22% margin, 9.88% cash deposit) came in far below the petition, but added to CVD (3.68-6.99% India; 103.49% China with preliminary critical circumstances, 09-24) the protection is still material.
